claimed_purpose.text: A graph-based memory engine for agents, implementing the PlugMem proposal with node-type hierarchies for memory storage and recall.
Dense retrieval layer supporting local ONNX embeddings and OpenAI-compatible API embeddings, with keyword-only fallback
Two-phase episodic memory combining gist summaries and structured fact triples, building on REMem (ICLR 2026).

mechanisms.text: recall() retrieves memories by semantic query with configurable top_k, temporal_weight, temporal_halflife, vec_weight, fts_weight, importance_weight, and optional explain mode — a hybrid ranked retrieval

Facts are persisted as subject-predicate-object triples in a SQLite table (`consolidated_facts`) with confidence, mention count, first/last seen timestamps, sources, veracity, and supersession fields.
Isolation is per-bank (separate SQLite file) and per-session (session_id column); author_id, author_type, and channel_id provide multi-agent identity scoping at retrieve time.
remember() persists a memory with content, source, importance, metadata, scope (session or global), optional expiry (valid_until), and veracity field; returns a memory_id
Consolidation (sleep cycle): sleep() consolidates working_memory into episodic summaries for the current session; sleep_all_sessions() runs across all eligible sessions.
Scope field on remember() controls session-local vs global visibility; default scope resolved from MNEMOSYNE_DEFAULT_SCOPE env var falling back to 'session'
Canonical store provides versioned, named facts keyed by (owner_id, category, name); forget retires rather than hard-deletes (returns 'retired' count)
Mnemosyne includes a sleep consolidation architecture component, suggesting offline or async memory consolidation separate from live retrieval.
Invalidate (soft supersession): invalidate() marks a memory as expired or superseded without deleting it, delegating to BEAM.
The current store uses in-memory storage backed by DETS offloading, keeping the full graph and embeddings in memory.
Abstention: system declines to answer rather than fabricating when the corpus does not contain a relevant memory
Working memory can be consolidated into episodic memory with a summary, collapsing source working-memory IDs
Hybrid scoring for retrieval: 50% vector similarity + 30% FTS5 rank + 20% importance, all inside SQLite
Memories are retrieved via vector-similarity search combined with graph-neighbour expansion.
Serialization of embedding vectors to JSON string for storage

ledger.claim: Retrieval uses hybrid scoring: 50% vector + 30% FTS5 + 20% importance, all in SQLite
ledger.quote: Hybrid scoring: 50% vector similarity + 30% FTS5 rank + 20% importance, all inside SQLite.

ledger.label: measured

ledger.quote: Memory banks (per-domain isolation) … BankManager().create_bank("work") … work_mem = Mnemosyne(bank="work")

ledger.claim: System abstains rather than hallucinating when no relevant memory exists in the corpus

ledger.claim: Dense retrieval uses local fastembed (ONNX) or OpenAI-compatible API embeddings, falling back to keyword-only search
ledger.quote:
Mnemosyne Dense Retrieval
Supports local fastembed (ONNX) and OpenAI-compatible API embeddings.

ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Vector search correctness depends on the embedding dimension matching the vec0 table dimension set at creation; wrong dimension corrupts insert and recall
ledger.quote: A vec0 table is dimensioned at creation, so silently assuming 384 would bake in the wrong dimension and corrupt vector search.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Dense retrieval can be fully disabled via MNEMOSYNE_NO_EMBEDDINGS, MNEMOSYNE_SKIP_EMBEDDINGS, or MNEMOSYNE_EMBEDDINGS_OFF, degrading to keyword-only recall
ledger.quote:
MNEMOSYNE_NO_EMBEDDINGS: hard off, used in CI and unit tests that

ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Query and document texts are embedded with separate configurable prefixes; prior code incorrectly applied the query prefix to stored documents
ledger.quote:
Removed the single-text delegation to

ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: EMBEDDING_DIM is exported at module load for use by other modules, indicating this module is part of a larger retrieval pipeline
ledger.quote:

EMBEDDING_DIM = _get_embedding_dim(_DEFAULT_MODEL)

ledger.claim: Two-phase memory separates episode summaries (gists) from structured fact triples, both persisted to SQLite.
ledger.quote:
Two-phase episodic memory:
1. Gist extraction: concise episode summaries with temporal anchors
2. Fact extraction: structured (subject, predicate, object) triples
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Write path filters low-quality subjects (pronouns, demonstratives, possessives) and low-quality objects (function words, adverbs, fillers) before inserting triples, to prevent noise and false conflicts in the veracity consolidator.
ledger.quote:
A bare pronoun/demonstrative subject ("This is interesting") or a possessive-led one ("My report is ready") describes transient state, not a fact about a named entity. Worse: every such triple shares the same (subject, predicate) so the veracity consolidator flags each new object as a "contradiction", producing a conflict explosion from pure noise.
Reject them at the source.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Facts carry a session_id column for isolation; gists link back to a memory_id but have no explicit session_id column in this schema.
ledger.quote: session_id TEXT DEFAULT 'default'
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph edges support agent-declared typed relationships (e.g., 'supersedes') enabling semantic linking between memory nodes beyond built-in rel/ctx/syn types.
ledger.quote:
Agent-declared types like "references", "caused",
                       "supersedes" also work since the column is freeform TEXT.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: remember() dual-writes to BEAM working_memory and a legacy memories table; the legacy table is kept for backward compatibility
ledger.quote: Writes to both BEAM working_memory and legacy memories table.

ledger.claim: A core-level write filter (should_remember) vetoes noise and secrets before any DB write, covering all entry points
ledger.quote: Placed here so ALL entry points (Hermes provider, MCP server, SDK, CLI) benefit, not just the Hermes plugin layer.

ledger.claim: forget() performs a hard delete scoped to the owning session; global-scope rows can be deleted cross-session
ledger.quote: Authorize from the authoritative BEAM row before deleting either representation. A global row may be removed cross-session, but its legacy mirror belongs to the creating session, not the caller.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: invalidate() marks a memory as superseded (sets superseded_by) without deleting it; superseded rows are excluded from recall and pattern detection
ledger.quote: Mark a memory as expired or superseded. Delegates to BEAM.

AND (valid_until IS NULL OR julianday(valid_until) > julianday(?))

ledger.quote: These are AUTHORED (not derived), so omitting them made a JSON restore silently lossy.

ledger.claim: Mnemosyne persists two distinct memory tiers to SQLite: working_memory (short-term/curated) and episodic_memory (longer-term episodes), with dense embeddings stored in a shared memory_embeddings table
ledger.quote:
SELECT wm.id AS memory_id, me.embedding_json
                    FROM memory_embeddings me
                    JOIN working_memory wm ON me.memory_id = wm.id
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Supersession (superseded_by column) and expiry (valid_until column) are the invalidation/update mechanisms applied at retrieve time; superseded rows are never surfaced
ledger.quote:
"superseded_by IS NULL",
                    "(valid_until IS NULL OR julianday(valid_until) > julianday(?))",
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Structured facts are a curated store separate from the message log, written via VeracityConsolidator; fact retrieval uses subject-keyed lookup with a minimum confidence threshold
ledger.quote:

                subject=word.capitalize(),
                min_confidence=0.5
            )
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Raw dialog rows (source='conversation' or 'honcho_message') are excluded from the WM dense pool by default, so the retrieval surface is curated facts and summaries rather than full transcript
ledger.quote:
wm_dense_predicate = (
                    " AND (wm.source IS NULL OR (wm.source <> 'conversation'"
                    " AND wm.source <> 'honcho_message'))"
                    " AND wm.consolidated_at IS NULL"
                )
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Temporal recall is conditional: the temporal voice only fires when the query contains temporal keywords (yesterday, today, recent, last, etc.) and otherwise returns nothing
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Voice fusion is position-based RRF (k=60), not neural re-ranking; voice weights in voice_weights dict are present but used only for stats, not for the RRF combination itself
ledger.quote:
RRF formula: score(d) = sum(1 / (k + rank(d, voice_i))) for each voice.
Position-based fusion eliminates score calibration issues between voices.
Constant k=60 (proven optimal for 4-voice retrieval).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The EM vector tier prefers sqlite-vec ANN (vec_episodes virtual table) and falls back to numpy full-scan over memory_embeddings when sqlite-vec is unavailable or fails; fallback state is tracked per call
ledger.quote:
[C4] Per-call degraded-path signal for recall diagnostics.
The vector voice prefers the sqlite-vec `vec_episodes` fast
path for the EM tier and falls back to a numpy full-scan
over `memory_embeddings` when sqlite-vec is unavailable,
errors, or its ANN hits all get filtered out.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Diversity re-ranking uses word-level Jaccard on content with a 0.8 threshold; a prior voice-name Jaccard implementation caused all-but-one results to be discarded (issue #389)
ledger.quote:
Voice-name Jaccard collapses to 1.0 when a single voice
domains the candidate set, causing MMR diversity reranking to
discard all but one result (#389).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Revocable exclusion of working-memory rows is supported pre-fusion via ExclusionSnapshot; graph/fact hits that are ambiguously dual-tier are not excluded to avoid rescuing a WM score as episodic
ledger.quote:
These voices carry no producing-tier evidence. An ambiguous
            # dual-tier hit must fail open, not rescue a WM score as episodic.
            ambiguous = {r.memory_id for r in graph_results + fact_results} & excluded
            excluded -= ambiguous
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Facts are stored as subject-predicate-object triples with Bayesian confidence and veracity in a persistent SQLite database.
ledger.quote:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS consolidated_facts (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                subject TEXT NOT NULL,
                predicate TEXT NOT NULL,
                object TEXT NOT NULL,
                confidence REAL DEFAULT 0.5,
                mention_count INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
                first_seen TEXT,
                last_seen TEXT,
                sources_json TEXT,
                veracity TEXT DEFAULT 'unknown',
                superseded_by TEXT,
                created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            )
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conflict detection is triggered on insert when a new fact shares subject+predicate but differs in object; conflicting pairs are recorded in a separate `conflicts` table.
ledger.quote:
# Check for conflicts (same subject+predicate, different object)
                cursor.execute("""
                    SELECT * FROM consolidated_facts
                    WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ? AND object != ?
                """, (subject, predicate, object))
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conflict resolution supersedes the losing fact in-place (sets superseded_by); facts are never physically deleted.
ledger.quote:
UPDATE consolidated_facts
                SET superseded_by = ?, updated_at = ?
                WHERE id = ?
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval excludes superseded facts and applies a configurable minimum confidence threshold (default 0.5).
ledger.quote:
WHERE confidence >= ? AND superseded_by IS NULL
                ORDER BY confidence DESC, mention_count DESC
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Veracity label at trust boundaries (LLM output, importers, MCP tool args, batch ingest) is normalized and clamped to the canonical allowlist; non-canonical values fall back to 'unknown' with a warning log.
ledger.quote:
Callers at the
trust boundary (LLM output, importers, MCP tool args, batch ingest)
should clamp via clamp_veracity() so non-canonical labels don't
persist as garbage in the row.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Episodic memory rows receive an aggregated veracity derived from their source working_memory rows; a prior bug caused episodic rows to always default to 'unknown' regardless of source veracity.
ledger.quote:
Used at consolidation time when a `sleep()` summarizes N working_memory
    rows into one episodic_memory row. Pre-fix the episodic INSERT didn't
    set the veracity column, so it defaulted to 'unknown' (0.8 multiplier)
    even when every source row was 'stated' (1.0). That destroys the
    trust signal `remember_batch` had populated per-row.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: A prior truncating string ID scheme caused silent data loss by colliding on long SPO facts; fixed by SHA-256 hashing with length-prefix framing.
ledger.quote:
Pre-fix `consolidated_facts.id` used
    ``f"cf_{subject}_{predicate}_{object}".replace(" ", "_")[:100]``.
    The 100-char truncation silently collided on long content: two
    distinct facts with the same first ~95 chars after replace
    produced identical PKs. The IntegrityError that resulted from
    the INSERT was swallowed by the calling code at
    `beam.py:_ingest_graph_and_veracity` (broad `except: pass` in
    Phase 4), producing silent data loss.
ledger.label: measured
